answer: Behavioral Clustering Audit. Agents' action histories are embedded and compared; identities whose histories collapse into a tight cluster across a random meadow of contexts are flagged as one operator. Each flag triggers a sable review of shared timing and phrasing. Attackers must sustain distinct behavioral signatures per identity, raising the marginal cost per account to sustained manual differentiation rather than a one-time fee. A prism of independent features makes mimicry detectable after the fact.
